The main takeaway from our work is that

Merlin, a protein that is mutated in a rare form of cancer, is a key player in a process known as contact-dependent inhibition of growth, and that this process is mediated by the ability of Merlin to restrain the epidermal growth receptor (EGFR), a cell surface molecule, to the membrane.

Nf2/merlin is a membrane/cyto-skeleton associated protein that is required for cell-cell contact-dependent inhibition of growth, and this is mediated by its ability to restrain the epidermal growth-factor receptor (EGFR), a membrane protein, into a membrane compartment where it can neither signal to the cytoplasm nor be endocytosed.
